answer: Before placing fill, an engineering analysis must demonstrate compensatory storage at least equal to the volume of the fill below the DFE. The replacement storage must be hydraulically connected to the affected area, within the same drainage reach, and available before placement; the analysis must also show that flood levels on other property will not increase. The Section 6.2 requirements do not apply to landscaping that changes elevation by no more than 0.05 metres over no more than 50 square metres and does not obstruct an identified drainage path.
question: What must be demonstrated before fill is placed in a designated Flood Storage Area, and when does the minor-landscaping exception apply?
exceptions: Section 6.3 exempts qualifying minor landscaping from the requirements in Section 6.2. The exception applies only when the elevation change is no more than 0.05 metres, the affected area is no greater than 50 square metres, and no identified drainage path is obstructed. No other exception is identified in the source text.
source_text:
Flood Storage Area Development Policy
6.1 Applicability. This section applies to development involving the placement of fill within a designated Flood Storage Area.
6.2 Compensatory storage. Fill may be placed only when an engineering analysis demonstrates that compensatory storage will provide at least the same volume as the proposed fill below the Design Flood Elevation. The replacement storage must be hydraulically connected to the affected storage area, located within the same drainage reach, and available before the fill is placed. The analysis must also demonstrate that the proposal will not increase flood levels on other property. These requirements are intended to preserve flood storage capacity and avoid transferring flood impacts to others.
6.3 Minor landscaping exception. The requirements in 6.2 do not apply to landscaping that changes ground elevation by no more than 0.05 metres over an area no greater than 50 square metres, provided the work does not obstruct an identified drainage path.
cited_provisions: Sections 6.1, 6.2, and 6.3. Section 6.2 specifies the compensatory-storage and no-increase-in-flood-level findings; Section 6.3 states the minor-landscaping exception and its limits.
compliance_basis: The applicable compliance obligation is to satisfy Section 6.2 unless the work meets every condition for the limited exception in Section 6.3. The source states that the compensatory-storage and impact-analysis requirements preserve flood storage capacity and avoid transferring flood impacts to others.
restriction_conditions: Fill may be placed only if compensatory storage below the DFE is at least equal in volume to the fill, is hydraulically connected to the affected area, is within the same drainage reach, and is available before the fill is placed. An engineering analysis must demonstrate that the proposal will not increase flood levels on other property. Landscaping outside the stated limits or obstructing an identified drainage path does not qualify for the exception.
applicability_requirements: The policy applies to development involving placement of fill within a designated Flood Storage Area. The minor-landscaping exception is limited to work meeting all three conditions in Section 6.3: a ground-elevation change of no more than 0.05 metres, an area of no more than 50 square metres, and no obstruction of an identified drainage path.

question: What elevation and construction requirements apply to a new residential building in the mapped Flood Fringe, and is any accessory structure exempt from the floor-elevation standard?
answer: The lowest occupied floor and electrical and mechanical equipment and service connections must be at least 0.6 metres above the DFE. Below that elevation, flood-damage-resistant materials are required, and basements and habitable floors are prohibited below the DFE. A detached, non-habitable accessory structure of no more than 18.6 square metres may be exempt from the floor-elevation standard if it is securely anchored, has flood openings, stores no hazardous materials, and is not used for sleeping; the other applicable requirements remain in effect.
exceptions: Section 4.4 provides a conditional exception from the floor-elevation standard for qualifying detached, non-habitable accessory structures of 18.6 square metres or less. It does not exempt them from the other applicable requirements in Section 4.3.
source_text:
Floodplain Development Standard
4.2 Applicability. Sections 4.3 and 4.4 apply to new residential buildings and substantial improvements located in the mapped Flood Fringe.
4.3 Residential elevation and construction. The lowest occupied floor must be at least 0.6 metres above the Design Flood Elevation (DFE). Electrical and mechanical equipment and service connections must also be placed at least 0.6 metres above the DFE. Areas below that elevation must use flood-damage-resistant materials, and no basement or habitable floor may be located below the DFE. These measures are intended to reduce risks to occupants and limit flood damage.
4.4 Accessory-structure exception. A detached, non-habitable accessory structure with a floor area no greater than 18.6 square metres is not required to meet the floor-elevation standard in 4.3 if it is securely anchored, has flood openings, stores no hazardous materials, and is not used for sleeping. All other applicable requirements in 4.3 remain in effect.
cited_provisions: Sections 4.2, 4.3, and 4.4. Section 4.3 requires the lowest occupied floor and specified equipment to be at least 0.6 metres above the DFE and prohibits basements or habitable floors below the DFE. Section 4.4 sets out the accessory-structure exception and its conditions.
compliance_basis: Compliance requires meeting the elevation and construction standards in Section 4.3, subject only to the limited exception and conditions in Section 4.4. The source states that these measures are intended to reduce risks to occupants and limit flood damage.
restriction_conditions: The lowest occupied floor and electrical and mechanical equipment and service connections must be at least 0.6 metres above the DFE. Below that elevation, flood-damage-resistant materials must be used; basements and habitable floors are prohibited below the DFE. An accessory structure qualifies for the floor-elevation exception only if it is securely anchored, has flood openings, stores no hazardous materials, and is not used for sleeping.
applicability_requirements: Sections 4.3 and 4.4 apply to new residential buildings and substantial improvements in the mapped Flood Fringe. The exception applies only to a detached, non-habitable accessory structure with a floor area no greater than 18.6 square metres that meets every condition in Section 4.4.
